question: What average interest rate did IDA-eligible countries face on new commitments in 2025, and how does that compare with the past?
answer: IDA-eligible countries faced an average interest rate of **8.2 percent** on new commitments from private creditors in 2025—up 0.6 percentage point from 2024 and the highest rate since 1989. [para:idr-2026:p0065:001]

events.query: IDA-eligible countries average interest rate new commitments 2025 compared past
events.context:
[para:idr-2026:p0065:001] (page 65; text)
The restoration of access to capital markets has come at a higher cost for public sector entities in IDA-eligible countries, however. Although the average interest rate on new commitments from official creditors has remained relatively steady at 2.7 percent over the 2024–25 period, the average rate on new commitments from private creditors continued to increase in 2025, to 8.2 percent, up 0.6 percentage point from 2024. Such elevated interest rates have not been seen since 1989 for public sector entities in this group of countries, when rates spiked in reaction to the 1980s debt crisis.

[para:idr-2026:p0020:001] (page 20; text)
• The countries that can least afford it are paying the most to borrow. Increased borrowing from private creditors hardened lending terms disproportionately for IDA-eligible countries, which faced an average interest rate of 8.2 percent on new commitments during the year, the highest since the late 1980s. The difference in interest rates that this group of borrowers pays when borrowing from official creditors and rates on debt from private creditors widened significantly over the past decade, from 3.4 percentage points in 2016 to 5.5 percentage points in 2025. International Bank for Reconstruction and Development borrowers, by contrast, saw improvements in the terms on new commitments, with an improved 5.5 percent average interest rate, down from 5.8 percent the previous year.

[para:idr-2026:p0051:001] (page 51; text)
As IDA-eligible countries continued to tap international markets to issue new bonds, they needed to pay even higher interest rates to attract investors to these instruments. Average interest rates on external commitments of IDA-eligible countries to bondholders increased 1.0 percentage point in 2025 to 9.4 percent, and remained above rates of IBRD borrowers, which experienced a decrease of 0.3 percentage point to 5.5 percent (figure 1.11). The return of international investors to IDA-eligible countries remains uneven, concentrated in the largest borrowers, and costly, as international investors have increased their search for yield. IDA borrowers have therefore absorbed global financial shocks disproportionately.

[para:idr-2026:p0051:000] (page 51; text)
Increased borrowing from private creditors has affected country lending groups disproportionately and has led to a hardening of the average terms of new loan commitments to IDA-eligible countries.
